newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Israeli attends a Mediterranean meeting in Tunis.
newsitem.headline: Israeli attends a Mediterranean meeting in Tunis.

text.p: An Israeli representative on Thursday attended a meeting in Tunis co-organised by the European Commission and a Tunisian state-controlled agency.
But Tunisian co-organisers said the invitation was sent to Israel by the European Commission last September -- months before an Arab League recommendation to freeze relations with the Jewsih state.
The Arab League, angered by Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, made the recommendation at a meeting in Cairo on Monday.
"It was necessary for me to be here, despite some hesitations. Trade ties are key for the (Middle East) peace process," Elizabeth Zvili, an executive at Israel Export Institute, told Reuters.

"The invitation was at our demand and we had strongly insisted to (Tunisian) Agence de Promotion de l'Investissement that Israel be invited," European Commission representative Anne Charlotte Bournoville said.
"The meeting is open to all EU members and the 12 Mediterranean countries, whatever the political divergences," she added.
The meeting is an EU initiative aimed at encouraging cooperation between the EU and Mediterranean countries.
Tunisia and Israel last year formally established low-level diplomatic relations by opening interests offices in Tunis and Tel Aviv.

The Tunisian government, which repeatedly said that ties with Israel were linked to progress in the peace process, has not yet announced what course of action it would take to implement Monday's Arab League recommendation.
